title: Micha Klein, Artificial Beauty “Venus”
lede: A digitally built portrait from Micha Klein’s 1998 series Artificial Beauties: a flawless face in front of floating 3D crystals, lens flares, and electric color.
summary: An idealised digital portrait against purple 3D crystals and neon light streaks. Micha Klein, 1998, Cibachrome on aluminium.

source.label: Kunsthuizen: Micha Klein, Arteficial beauty Venus

evidence.note: Inspected the image on the Kunsthuizen art-lending page for this print (840 × 864, series no. 5 of the edition), in a scratchpad copy. Not stored.

styles.note: Partial fit: late-1990s digital-render imagery with 3D crystals, lens flares, and electric purple, blue, and pink. It has no chrome, plastic, or type.

context: Kunsthuizen describes an original 1998 photograph from Klein’s series Artificial Beauties, as exhibited at the Groninger Museum: a Cibachrome print on aluminium behind perspex, 75 × 75 cm. [Kunsthuizen](https://www.kunsthuizen.nl/kunstwerken/venus-micha-klein/).

Klein (1964–2026) studied at the Gerrit Rietveld Academie and graduated in 1989 with the first degree there in computer graphics. The Groninger Museum held a ten-year retrospective of his digital work in 1998. [Micha Klein: About](https://www.michaklein.com/about); [Digicult (2006)](https://digicult.it/digimag/issue-014/the-multimedia-colours-of-micha-klein/); [Metropolis M](https://metropolism.com/nl/feature/i-m-micha-klein-1964-2026/).
observed: A woman with red hair and bare shoulders faces the viewer; her skin is smooth and even, like a retouched render.
Behind her float faceted purple and violet crystals of different sizes, some translucent.
The background swirls with electric blue, cyan, magenta, and orange streaks and fractal-like filaments.
Small star-shaped lens flares sparkle at the lower left and upper right.
interpretation: This is the image side of Y2K: 3D software used for its own sake, with rendered crystals, flares, and a perfected artificial face. The Y2K style record cites Evan Collins, [in the Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2016/may/19/year-2000-y2k-millennium-design-aesthetic), linking the aesthetic to new CAD tools that allowed layered transparencies and lens flares.
The palette of violet, electric blue, and hot pink matches the style’s accent colors.
borrow: Use a few floating rendered crystals or gems with sharp facets as background motifs.
Add small four-point sparkle flares at the corners of an image.

rights.statement: No image is stored. The work is © the estate of Micha Klein.
